# ng-ql

> An Eloquent-inspired HTTP request and query builder for Angular. It is **not an ORM** — it manages no database, no models, no identity map. It builds, serializes, executes, types, caches, and exposes HTTP requests against REST APIs using Angular `HttpClient`, Signals, and RxJS.

Runtime dependencies: `@angular/core`, `@angular/common`, `rxjs` only. Angular 21+.

## Install

```bash
npm install ng-ql
```

## Provider setup

```ts
import { provideHttpClient } from '@angular/common/http';
import { provideNgQl } from 'ng-ql';

bootstrapApplication(AppComponent, {
  providers: [
    provideHttpClient(),
    provideNgQl({
      baseUrl: 'https://api.example.com/v1',
      defaultHeaders: { Accept: 'application/json' },
      withCredentials: false,
      defaultCachePolicy: 'no-store',   // default for Signal reads that don't specify one
      defaultCacheTtl: 60_000,          // ms
      // querySerializer: custom NgQlQuerySerializer   (optional)
      // responseAdapter: custom NgQlResponseAdapter   (optional)
    }),
  ],
});
```

`baseUrl` is joined onto relative endpoints without duplicate/missing slashes. An endpoint starting with `http://`, `https://`, or `//` is treated as absolute and used as-is (never prefixed).

## Defining a resource

A model is a plain `interface` — no base class, no decorators. A resource extends `NgQlResource<TModel, TId>` and is injectable like any other service:

```ts
export interface Post {
  id: number;
  title: string;
  status: 'draft' | 'published' | 'archived';
}

@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class PostResource extends NgQlResource<Post, number> {
  constructor(client: NgQlClient) {
    super(client, { endpoint: 'posts', cacheTags: ['posts'] });
  }
}
```

`NgQlResourceConfig` fields: `endpoint` (required), `primaryKey`, `mapItem`/`mapCollection`/`mapPaginated` (per-resource response overrides), `buildUrl`, `requestOptions`, `headers`, `cacheTags`.

IMPORTANT: `NgQlResource`'s constructor takes `(client: NgQlClient, config: NgQlResourceConfig<TModel, TId>)` via plain constructor injection (not `inject()`), specifically so subclasses can pass `client` through `super(...)`. Do not "fix" this to use `inject()` — it is intentional.

## Query builder — immutable, no request until executed

Every chain method on `NgQlQueryBuilder<TModel, TId>` returns a **new** instance; nothing is ever mutated. **No HTTP request is made** until an execution method (`get`, `first`, `paginate`, `find`, or a `*Signal` twin) is called.

```ts
this.posts
  .query()
  .where('status', 'published')          // shorthand: field, value  => equality
  .where('price', '>=', 100)              // explicit operator: field, operator, value
  .where({ title: 'Hello', name: 'Test' }) // object form: every entry AND-ed together
  .orWhere('featured', true)              // ORs a new group against everything before it
  .orWhere({ role: 'admin', active: true }) // object form works on orWhere too
  .whereIn('categoryId', [1, 2])
  .whereNotIn('authorId', [9])
  .whereNull('deletedAt')
  .whereNotNull('publishedAt')
  .whereBetween('price', [10, 20])
  .when(someCondition, (q) => q.where('featured', true))
  .select(['id', 'title'])
  .with('author')                          // or with(['author', 'comments'])
  .withQuery({ custom: 'param' })          // alias: append(...)
  .orderBy('createdAt', 'desc')            // or latest('createdAt') / oldest('createdAt')
  .limit(10)
  .offset(20)
  .page(2, 20)                             // page number, per-page size
  .perPage(20)
  .setHeaders({ 'X-Foo': 'bar' })
  .setOptions({ withCredentials: true })
  .get()                                   // Observable<TModel[]>
  .subscribe((posts) => console.log(posts));
```

Supported operators for the explicit `where(field, operator, value)` form: `'=' | '!=' | '<>' | '>' | '>=' | '<' | '<=' | 'like' | 'not like'`.

`where`/`orWhere` grouping: consecutive `where(...)` calls AND together into the current group; `orWhere(...)` starts a new group OR-ed against everything before it. `where(a).where(b).orWhere(c).where(d)` groups as `(a AND b) OR (c AND d)`. With no `orWhere` anywhere in the chain, this is invisible — output is a single flat `filter[...]` group, unchanged. As soon as one `orWhere` appears, every group (including the first) is nested under `filter[or][<groupIndex>]` (see the wire-format section below).

Invalid inputs (`NaN`, negative `limit`/`offset`, `page` < 1, `perPage` < 1, an unrecognized operator string) throw `NgQlValidationError` synchronously at the chain-call site — before any request, without needing to subscribe.

### Observable execution methods

```ts
query.get(options?)                          // Observable<TModel[]>
query.first(options?)                        // Observable<TModel | null>  (null if empty)
query.paginate(page?, perPage?, options?)    // Observable<NgQlPaginatedResponse<TModel>>
query.find(id, options?)                     // Observable<TModel | null>
```

### Signal execution methods

Must be called from an injection context (a field initializer, a constructor, or inside `runInInjectionContext(...)`) because they call `inject(DestroyRef)` internally for lifecycle-safe cleanup.

```ts
query.getSignal(options?)                        // NgQlRequestState<TModel[]>
query.firstSignal(options?)                      // NgQlRequestState<TModel | null>
query.paginateSignal(page?, perPage?, options?)  // NgQlPaginatedRequestState<TModel>
```

```ts
protected readonly postsState = this.posts
  .query()
  .where('status', 'published')
  .orderBy('createdAt', 'desc')
  .getSignal({ cache: 'stale-while-revalidate', cacheTtl: 30_000 });

// postsState.data() / .loading() / .error() / .status() / .hasData()
// postsState.refresh()    -- re-executes, bypassing cache-first shortcut, still writes cache
// postsState.invalidate() -- drops the cache entry, resets state to 'idle'

protected readonly postsPage = this.posts.query().paginateSignal(1, 10);
// postsPage.data() / .meta() / .links() / .setPage(2) / .setPerPage(25)  -- these REPLACE data()

// Infinite-scroll / "load more": appends instead of replacing.
// postsPage.hasMore() / .loadingMore() (distinct from .loading())
// postsPage.loadMore() -- no-op while already loading, or once hasMore() is false
```

`status` is one of `'idle' | 'loading' | 'success' | 'error'`. All public signals are read-only.

Every Signal state (both `NgQlRequestState` and `NgQlPaginatedRequestState`) also has
`mutateOptimistically(updater, commit)` for optimistic UI: applies `updater` to the current data
immediately, subscribes to `commit()`, and — only on error — restores the previous value/status
and surfaces the error via `.error()`. Does not touch the cache (a mutation's own cache
invalidation already governs what a later `refresh()` sees).

```ts
postsState.mutateOptimistically(
  (posts) => (posts ?? []).filter((p) => p.id !== id),
  () => this.posts.destroy(id),
);
```

### Inspection methods (never trigger a request)

```ts
query.toUrl(): string
query.toQueryParams(): HttpParams
query.toRequest(): NgQlRequestDescription   // { method, url, params, headers, withCredentials?, body? }
```

## Resource convenience methods

```ts
resource.query(): NgQlQueryBuilder<TModel, TId>
resource.all(options?): Observable<TModel[]>
resource.allSignal(options?): NgQlRequestState<TModel[]>
resource.find(id, options?): Observable<TModel | null>
resource.findSignal(id, options?): NgQlRequestState<TModel | null>
resource.first(options?): Observable<TModel | null>
resource.firstSignal(options?): NgQlRequestState<TModel | null>
resource.create(payload: Partial<TModel>, options?): Observable<TModel>
resource.update(id, payload: Partial<TModel>, options?): Observable<TModel>   // PUT
resource.patch(id, payload: Partial<TModel>, options?): Observable<TModel>   // PATCH
resource.destroy(id, options?): Observable<void>                            // DELETE
resource.getId(model: TModel): TId    // reads model[primaryKey ?? 'id']
```

Every successful `create`/`update`/`patch`/`destroy` automatically invalidates cache entries owned by that resource's endpoint, plus any of the resource's configured `cacheTags`. Mutations are never cached themselves.

## Caching policies (`NgQlCachePolicy`)

Only relevant to the `*Signal` methods (`NgQlSignalRequestOptions` extends `NgQlRequestOptions` with `cache`, `cacheTtl`, `cacheKey`, `cacheTags`, `retry`, `retryDelay`). Plain Observable methods always hit the network.

| Policy | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `'no-store'` | Always executes the request; never reads or writes the cache. |
| `'cache-first'` | Returns valid cached data immediately if present; otherwise fetches. |
| `'network-first'` | Fetches fresh data first; falls back to a cached value if the request fails. |
| `'stale-while-revalidate'` | Returns cached data immediately (if any) while revalidating in the background. |

Cache keys are deterministic (method + resolved URL + normalized, order-independent params/headers/body), so equivalent query builders always hit the same cache entry regardless of chain order. Concurrent identical in-flight `GET`s are always deduplicated into one HTTP call, regardless of policy.

`NgQlCacheService` (injectable, instance-scoped — never global/static) also exposes `invalidateKey(key)`, `invalidateTag(tag)`, `invalidateEndpoint(endpoint)`, `clear()`.

### Retries

`retry` (default `0`, disabled) and `retryDelay` (default `300`ms) on `NgQlSignalRequestOptions` retry a failed network attempt with exponential backoff (`retryDelay * 2^(attempt-1)`) *before* the policy's fallback/error kicks in — pairs naturally with `network-first`. Concurrent identical requests share a single retry sequence.

```ts
this.posts.query().getSignal({ cache: 'network-first', retry: 2, retryDelay: 300 });
```

## Header precedence (ascending — later wins)

1. `NgQlConfig.defaultHeaders`
2. `NgQlResourceConfig.headers`
3. `NgQlQueryBuilder#setHeaders(...)`
4. Per-call `options.headers`

## Response shapes the default adapter understands

- Raw array: `[{...}, {...}]`
- `{ data: [{...}, {...}] }`
- `{ data: {...} }` or a raw item object
- Paginated: `{ data: [...], meta: { current_page | currentPage, last_page | lastPage, per_page | perPage, total }, links?: { first, last, prev, next } }`

Override globally via `provideNgQl({ responseAdapter })`, or per-resource via `NgQlResourceConfig.mapItem/mapCollection/mapPaginated`.

## Default query-serializer wire format

```text
where('status', 'published')        => filter[status]=published
where('price', '>=', 100)           => filter[price][gte]=100
whereIn('categoryId', [1, 2])       => filter[categoryId][]=1&filter[categoryId][]=2
whereNotIn('categoryId', [1, 2])    => filter[categoryId][not_in][]=1&filter[categoryId][not_in][]=2
whereNull('deletedAt')              => filter[deletedAt]=null
whereNotNull('deletedAt')           => filter[deletedAt][ne]=null
whereBetween('price', [10, 20])     => filter[price][between]=10,20
select(['id', 'title'])             => fields=id,title
with('author')                      => include=author
orderBy('createdAt', 'desc')        => sort=-createdAt
limit(10)                           => page[size]=10
offset(20)                          => page[offset]=20
page(2, 20)                         => page[number]=2&page[size]=20

where('status', 'published').orWhere('featured', true)
                                     => filter[or][0][status]=published&filter[or][1][featured]=true
```

Override globally via `provideNgQl({ querySerializer })` to match a different backend convention (OData, JSON:API, a bespoke dialect, ...).

## Testing (HttpTestingController)

```ts
TestBed.configureTestingModule({
  providers: [provideHttpClient(), provideHttpClientTesting(), provideNgQl({ baseUrl: '/api' }), PostResource],
});
const httpMock = TestBed.inject(HttpTestingController);
const posts = TestBed.inject(PostResource);

posts.all().subscribe();
httpMock.expectOne('/api/posts').flush([{ id: 1, title: 'Hello' }]);
httpMock.verify();
```

For Signal methods, call them inside `TestBed.runInInjectionContext(() => ...)`.

## SSR

No `window`, `document`, `localStorage`, or other browser globals anywhere in the library. Safe to instantiate once per server-rendered request.

## Common mistakes to avoid when generating code against ng-ql

- Do not treat `NgQlResource` as an ORM entity/model — it has no identity map, no change tracking, no `.save()`. It is only a typed façade over HTTP.
- Do not call `getSignal`/`firstSignal`/`paginateSignal`/`allSignal`/`findSignal` outside an injection context (they'll throw `NG0203`). Call them as field initializers or inside `runInInjectionContext`.
- Do not expect a plain `get()`/`first()`/`paginate()` (Observable) call to use the cache — only the `*Signal` methods cache, via `NgQlSignalRequestOptions`.
- Do not mutate a query builder in place or expect chain methods to affect the receiver — always use the returned value: `const q2 = q1.where(...)`, not `q1.where(...); use(q1)`.
- Do not assume `first()` throws on an empty result — it resolves to `null`.
- Do not hand-roll query strings — use the builder's `where*`/`select`/`with`/`orderBy`/`page` methods so the configured `NgQlQuerySerializer` stays in control of the wire format.
